title: Cofinality: approaching limits, regular and singular cardinals
summary: The number of positions needed to approach a limit distinguishes regular sizes from singular ones.
abstract: A long well-order can sometimes be approached using a much smaller collection of its positions. Cofinality measures the smallest size of a collection that reaches past every earlier position. Assuming the axiom of choice, an infinite size is regular when approaching it requires that many positions, and singular when fewer suffice. Every successor of an infinite cardinal is regular, but the limit of the first countably many infinite cardinals is singular. The same distinction determines whether a union of fewer, smaller sets must stay smaller.
